messages:
maria: FYI customer (AcmeRetail) escalated — streaming responses for long chat sessions suddenly cut off mid-stream and they were billed for 5xx. They sent a sample curl that reproduces: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate` — connection closes after ~2s of tokens. request_id=req_ABC123def, timeframe 2026-03-15T14:12:20Z

kai: thanks, can you paste the customer curl + headers? also curious if they're behind a proxy/load balancer.

maria: pasted their minimal repro below (they said no LB on their side):
```bash
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwft-7b-stream","prompt":"longchat"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

jen: saw a small spike of `client_disconnected` in streaming gateway around that window. metrics: streaming_disconnects +120% between 14:10-14:20 UTC.

leo: pulled logs for req_ABC123def: snippet below. looks like the client sent FIN then the upstream handler recorded a proxy error and surfaced 502.
```
[14:12:20Z] gateway: req=req_ABC123def conn=shared-proxy-7 read=200ms write=2100ms status=200 stream=true
[14:12:22Z] gateway: req=req_ABC123def recv: client EOF (read returned 0)
[14:12:22Z] upstream: req=req_ABC123def stream abort: upstream reset by peer
[14:12:22Z] billing: req=req_ABC123def classify=5xx reason=upstream_reset
```

maria: customer insists they didn't cancel client, they wait until full response and then socket closed prematurely. they attached tcpdump showing FIN from our side (but unclear).

kai: quick hypothesis: keepalive/heartbeat mismatch between our streaming proxy and the model workers — if worker sends FIN after upstream reset, proxy logs upstream_reset then billing rule increments 5xx. we currently treat any upstream reset during streaming as server 5xx.

sre-bot: No deploys to streaming-gateway in the 2h window prior to 14:12.

support-bot: Related tickets: #4321 (chunked-eof edgecases), #4478 (billing classification rules). linking.

jen: actionable repro we used locally: run the curl with `--no-buffer`, keep it idle for ~1.5s while the model emits, then force-close the client. In our test, proxy sometimes labels it `upstream_reset`. Repro snippet: `python -c "import sys,socket,time; s=socket.create_connection(('api.redwood.ai',443)); s.send(b'...'); time.sleep(1.6); s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RD); s.close()"` — yields same log pattern.

leo: short-term mitigation: change billing pipeline to check for downstream FIN/EOF before tagging as 5xx for streaming endpoints. that would avoid charging the customer for client-side aborts. I can open a patch for the classifier.

maria: please do and add a note to customer that we're investigating; ask them for full tcpdump + trace IDs. cc @kai @jen.

kai: follow-up for engineering: can we make gateway treat `recv: client EOF` as a client disconnect event (4xx/no-bill) not `upstream_reset` when streaming=true? this would avoid miscount. I can draft a small change: if downstream FIN observed within 500ms of upstream reset, mark as client_abort.

jen: looks good. also will add a transient alert suppression so this surge doesn't trigger paging while we triage. :thumbsup:

leo: opening internal ticket INF-2519 with logs + repro + proposed classifier patch. ETA for patch review: 24 hours. I will also add an integration test that simulates half-closed sockets and chunked sequence fragmentation.

maria: perfect. I'll reply to customer with interim note and ask for the additional tcpdump + exact SDK version. thanks team. :pray:
